84:1: God Almighty says: When the sky is split and torn apart and becomes doors.
84:2: And His statement: And she listened to her Lord and was right, meaning: And the heavens heard their Lord in their cracking and splitting, and they obeyed Him in His command to them. The Arabs say: He gave you permission in this matter, He gave you permission in this matter, meaning: He listened to you. And from this is the report that was narrated, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God did not listen to anything as He did to a prophet who chanted the Qur’an,” meaning by that: God did not listen to anything as He did to a prophet who chanted the Qur’an. And from this is the saying of the poet: Deaf when they hear good things mentioned to them, but when they hear bad things mentioned to them, they listen. The origin of their saying about obedience is: He listened to him from listening. It is said from it: I listened to you, meaning I heard what you said and obeyed what you said and commanded. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement, And she gave permission to her Lord, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And she listened to her Lord and fulfilled her duty, he said: She listened to her Lord. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, And she listened to her Lord and obeyed. He said: She heard and obeyed. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And she gave permission to her Lord and fulfilled her duty, he said: I heard. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, And she listened to her Lord and obeyed. He said: She heard and obeyed. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And she listened to her Lord and was obedient: meaning she heard and obeyed. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And she listened to her Lord and was right, he said: She heard and obeyed. His saying: And it was decreed means: God decreed that she should listen to the split and obey Him in that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: Amri told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and it was made obligatory, he said: It was made obedient to its Lord. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: And it was due and it was due to her.
84:3: And His saying: And when the earth is extended, God Almighty says: And when the earth is spread out, its breadth is increased. Like what Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali ibn Husayn, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will spread out the earth until there is no human being left except the space of his feet, and I will be the first to be called, and Gabriel will be on the right of the Most Merciful, and by God he had never seen him before, and I will say: O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me, and He will say: He spoke the truth, then I will intercede and say: O Lord, Your servants worshipped You at the ends of the earth, and he said: And it is the praised station.” Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, extended, he said: on the Day of Resurrection.
84:4: And His saying: And it cast out what was in it and became empty, God Almighty says: And the earth cast out what was in it of the dead to its back and became empty of them to God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and she threw out what was in it and emptied herself, he said: She took out what was in it of the dead. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And she threw out what was in it and emptied herself. He said: She took out her burdens and what was in it.
84:5: And His statement: And she listened to her Lord and was obliged to do so. He says: And the earth heard the command of her Lord in throwing out the dead from within her to the living from above, and obeyed. And was obliged to do so. He says: And God fulfilled it in listening to His command in that, and in fulfilling its duty to obey Him. The Arab scholars differed about the position of the answer to his statement, When the sky is split and his statement, When the earth is extended. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: When the sky is split has the meaning of his statement, O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with great striving and will meet Him, when the sky is split, in order of precedence and delay. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Some of the commentators said: The answer to When the sky is split is his saying: And it gives permission. He said: We see that he saw what the commentator saw, and he likened it to the saying of God Almighty: When they come to it and its gates are opened (al-Zumar 39:73) because we did not hear an answer with the waw in when it is a beginning, nor a statement before it, nor in when it is, when it begins. He said: The Arabs only answer with the waw in his saying: Until it was and When it was, they did not go beyond that. He said: The answer in When the sky is split and in When the earth is extended is like what is left out, because the specific is known and its meaning has been repeated in the Qur’an, so it is known. If you wish, its answer is: O man, like the saying of the one who says: If such and such is, then O people, you will see what you know of good or evil. You make O man the answer, and the fa is implied in it. The answer to When the sky is split has been explained as what a person receives of reward and punishment, so the meaning is as if: you will see the reward and punishment. If the sky splits. The correct statement in this regard, in our view, is that its answer has been omitted, leaving it to suffice with the knowledge of those addressed by it in its meaning. The meaning of the statement is: If the sky is split open, man will see what he has presented of good or evil. This is made clear by His statement, O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion and will meet Him, and the verses after it.
84:6: God Almighty says: O man, you are doing a deed for your Lord and will meet Him with it, whether your deed is good or bad. He says: So let your deed be among those that save you from His wrath and bring you His pleasure, and let it not be among those that anger Him with you and you will perish. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion and will meet Him. He says: You do a deed with which you will meet God, whether it is good or bad. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion and will meet Him. Indeed, your striving, O son of Adam, is weak, so whoever is able to make his striving in obedience to God, let him do so, and there is no power except with God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, you are striving toward your Lord with great striving, he said: Doing work for Him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and I heard him say about that: Indeed, you are striving towards your Lord with toil. He said: Work towards your Lord with work. He said: Toiling: work.
84:7: And His statement: But as for he who is given his book of deeds in his right hand, God Almighty says: But as for he who is given his book of deeds in his right hand.
84:8: God Almighty says: Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning, that is, his deeds will be looked at, his bad deeds will be forgiven, and he will be rewarded for his good deeds. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, and the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Wahid ibn Hamza, on the authority of Ibad ibn Abd God ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: O God, bring me to an easy reckoning. I said: O Messenger of God, what is an easy reckoning? He said: That his sins be looked at and overlooked, and whoever is questioned about the reckoning on that Day will be doomed. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said: Abd al-Wahid ibn Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of Ibad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say in some of his prayers: O God, judge me with an easy judgment. When he finished, I said: O Messenger of God, what is an easy judgment? He said: It is to look into his book and be forgiven for it. Whoever is questioned by the judge on that Day, O Aisha, will be doomed. Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us: Muslim told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Al-Kharit, the brother of Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Whoever is questioned about the account, or is brought to account, will be punished. Then she said: The account is only easy: it is presented to God while He sees them. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab told us, he said: Ayoub told us, and Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is brought to account on the Day of Resurrection will be punished. I said: Doesn’t God say: Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning? He said: That is not the reckoning, rather that is the presentation, but whoever is questioned about the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection will be punished. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Rawh ibn Ubadah told us: Abu Amir Al-Khazzaz told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except that he will be punished. I said: “Does God not say: ‘Then he will be called to account with an easy reckoning?’” He said: “That is the presentation. Whoever is called to account will be punished.” And he pointed with his hand to his finger as if he was poking it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning, he said: The easy reckoning is that which forgives his sins and accepts his good deeds, and the easy reckoning is that which is pardoned. And he recited, And they fear the evil of the reckoning (al-Ra’d 13:21), and he recited, Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, among the companions of Paradise (al-Ahqaf 46:16). Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, who said: Ibn Abi Malekah told us, on the authority of Aisha, who said: O Messenger of God, He will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. He said: That is the presentation, O Aisha. Whoever is called to account will perish. Ibn Bashar told us: Uthman bin Omar and Abu Dawud told us: Abu Amir Al-Khazzaz told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is brought to account will be punished. She said: “I said: Doesn’t God say: ‘Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning.’ He said: That is the presentation, O Aisha, and whoever is called to account will be punished.” If someone were to say: How is it said, Then he will be held accountable, while accountability can only be done by two people, and God is the One who takes care of their deeds, and no one has a claim before his Lord to hold him accountable? It would be said: That is God’s confirmation to the servant of his sins, and the servant’s admission of them, and of what his book of deeds has recorded. That is the accountability as we have described, and that is why it was said: He will be held accountable. Amr ibn Ali told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Abu Yunus al-Qushayri, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except that he will perish. She said: “So I said: O Messenger of God, ‘But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to account with an easy reckoning.’ He said: That is the presentation. No one will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection except that he will perish.”
84:9: And His saying: And he will return to his family, happy, means: And this person who will be held to account for an easy reckoning will return to his family in Paradise, happy. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And he returns to his family, rejoicing, he said: To the family for whom God has prepared Paradise.
84:10: God Almighty says: And as for he among you, O people, who is given his book on that Day behind his back, that is by placing his right hand to his neck, and placing his left hand behind his back, so he takes his book with his left hand from behind his back. And for this reason, the Most High described them as sometimes being given their books with their left hands, and sometimes as being given them from behind their backs. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, But as for he who is given his record behind his back, he said: He puts his hand behind his back.
84:11: And his saying: Then he will call for destruction, meaning: Then he will call for destruction, which is to say: Woe to me! Woe to me! It is from their saying: So-and-so called for his destruction, meaning: Woe to me! And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. We have mentioned the meaning of thawbur previously, with its evidence and the narrations that it contains. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, He calls for destruction, that he said: He calls for ruin.
84:12: And His statement: And he will be roasted in a Blaze. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Mecca, Medina, and Syria read it as and will be roasted, with a damma on the yaa' and a shaddah on the lam, meaning that God will roast them, roasting after roasting, and cooking after cooking, as God Almighty said: Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins. (An-Nisa': 56). They also cited as evidence to correct their recitation that His statement: Then they will roast in Hellfire. (al-Haqqah 69:31). Some of the Medinans and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as: And they will roast in it, with a fatha on the yaa' and a light lam, meaning that they will roast in it and return to it, and they will burn in it. They also cited as evidence to correct their recitation that God Almighty said: They will roast in it. (Ibrahim 14:29) and Except for he who is roasting in Hellfire. (al-Saffat 37:163). The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
84:13: And His statement: Indeed, he was happy among his family. God Almighty says: He was happy among his family in this world, because of his disobedience to God’s command and his committing of His sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, he was rejoicing among his family means in this world.
84:14: And His statement: "Indeed, he thought that he would never return. * Yes." God Almighty says: Indeed, this one who was given his book behind his back on the Day of Resurrection thought in this world that he would not return to us, and that he would not be resurrected after his death. So he did not care about the sins he committed, because he did not hope for reward, and he did not fear punishment. It is said from this: So-and-so turned away from this matter: if he turned away from it. And from this is the report that was narrated "from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to say in his supplication: O God, I seek refuge in You from weakness after strength." Meaning by that: from returning to disbelief, after faith. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He thought that he would never be resurrected, meaning: he would not be resurrected. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, “Indeed, he thought that he would never return to us. Yes.” He said: That he would not return to us. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He thought that he would never return means that he would have no resurrection or return. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: That he will not be transformed. He said: That he will not be turned over: he says: That he will not be resurrected. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, He thought that he would not change. He said: He would return. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, that it will not be changed, he said: that it will not be turned over.
84:15: And His saying: Yes, God Almighty says: Yes, he will surely be transformed and return to his Lord alive, as he was before his death. And His saying: His Lord was All-Seeing of him. God Almighty says: The Lord of this one who thought he would never be freed was All-Seeing of him, while he was in this world, with what sins he had committed therein, and what his affair would become in the Hereafter, knowing all of that.
84:16: This is an oath by our Lord, by the twilight. The twilight is the redness on the horizon from the west side of the sun, according to some of them. The interpreters differed on this. Some of them said: It is the redness, as we said. Among those who said this were a group of people from Iraq. Others said: It is the day. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told me: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us: Al-Awam ibn Hawshab told us: I said to Mujahid: The twilight. He said: “Do not say the twilight, for the twilight is from the sun, but say: the redness of the horizon.” Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: The twilight means the entire day. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, So I swear by the twilight, he said: the day. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: Twilight is the name for redness and whiteness, and they said: It is one of the opposites. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God swore by the day departing and the night approaching. As for the twilight at which the evening prayer is performed, we think it is red, for the reason we have explained in our book, The Book of Prayer.
84:17: And his statement: And the night and what it gathers, meaning: And the night and what it gathers, of what is still, and this includes what has a soul that flies or moves during the day. It is said from this: I gave him a watering-pot, and from this: food that is gathered in large containers or a vessel. And from this is the word wasq, which is the food gathered in large quantities that is measured or weighed. It is said: it is sixty sa’s, and this is what came in the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and what was gathered means: and what was collected. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: And the night and what it covers, he said: And what it gathers. And Ibn Abbas said: Shopkeepers, if they could find a driver Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: Hafs asked Al-Hasan about his statement, And the night and what it covers. He said: And what it gathers. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the night and what it covers. He said: And what it gathers means: what it shelters of animals. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And the night and what it covers means what it wraps. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And the night and what it covers. He said: And what is darkened over it, and what is brought into it. Ibn Abbas said: Shops if they could find a guide Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the night and what it covers, meaning: and what it gathers of stars or animals. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And what was gathered he said: And what was collected. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the night and what it covers, he said: And what is gathered, in which are gathered the things that God gathers, which take refuge in Him, and things that are in the night that are not in the day, what is gathered from what is in it what takes refuge in, is from what is gathered. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And the night and what it covers, meaning: what it wraps around. He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, And the night and what it covers. He said: And what is included in it. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr: And the night and what it covers: and what it gathers. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Nafi’ bin Omar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And what was gathered means what was collected. Haven’t you heard the poet say: Shops that could not find a driver Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And the night and what it covers, he said: What it covers when night comes. Others said: The meaning of this is: And what he drove. Who said that? Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Marwazi told us: Ali bin Al-Hassan told us: Hussein told us: I heard Ikrimah being asked, By the night and what it covers. He said: What it covers of darkness. So when night comes, everything goes to its home. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah: And the night and what it conceals. He said: What it drives of darkness. When night comes, it drives everything to its destination. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, And the night and what it covers, he said: What it drives with it of darkness when it comes. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the night and what it covers, meaning: And what the night covers of anything, the stars gather. And it is said: And the night and what it gathers.
84:18: And his saying: And by the moon when it is full, meaning: And by the moon when it is complete and straight. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the moon when it is full, meaning: when it is straight. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the moon when it is full, he said: when it is full and level. Hanad told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, And the moon when it is full, he said: when it is straight. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: Hafs asked Al-Hasan, about his statement, And the moon when it is full, he said: When it is full, when it is full. Abu Kudayna told me: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, And the moon when it is full, he said: on the thirteenth. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, When it is consistent, he said: When it is equal. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr: And the moon when it is full means when it is straight. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: If it becomes straight means if it becomes round. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the moon when it is full: when it is straight. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the moon when it is full, that he said: When it comes together and is straight. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the moon when it is full, he said: When it is straight.
84:19: And his saying: You will surely ascend from one level to another. The reciters differed in their recitation of it. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas`ud and his companions, Ibn Abbas and the majority of the reciters of Mecca and Kufa recited it la tarkaban with the ta’ and the ba’ open. The reciters of that also differed in its meaning. Some of them said: You will surely ascend, O Muhammad, from one state to another, and from one matter to another of the hardships. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Mujahid, that Ibn Abbas used to recite You will surely ascend from one level to another, meaning your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will ascend from one state to another. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding You will surely ascend from level to level, he said: One home after another. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: one state after another. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas You will surely ascend from level to level meaning: one house after another, and it is said: one matter after another, and one state after another. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said: I heard Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: One state after another. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: One state after another. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: Hafs asked Al-Hasan about his saying You will surely ascend from level to level, he said: Home to home, and state to state. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, he said: I was asked once about his saying You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: One state after another. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id: You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: One state after another. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: One state after another. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Nasr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: One situation after another. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement You will surely ascend from one level to another he said: You will ascend from one state to another. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement You will surely ascend from level to level means: state after state, and home after home. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: You will surely ascend from level to level, home after home, and state after state. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: One matter after another. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: One thing after another. Others who read this article and this reading said: What he meant by that is: You, Muhammad, will ascend from one heaven to another. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: You will surely ride meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, level upon level of the heavens. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: O Muhammad, from one sky to another. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Heaven after heaven. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: A sky above a sky. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: You will ride the Hereafter after the first. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement You will surely ascend from one level to another the latter after the first. Others who read this reading said: What is meant by that is that it changes in various ways, and is sometimes split by clouds, and sometimes turns red, and becomes rose-colored like oil, and sometimes like molten metal. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Wahb, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud You will surely ascend from one level to another He said: The sky is sometimes like paint, and sometimes it cracks. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: I heard Abu Al-Zarqa’ Al-Hamadani - and it is not Abu Al-Zarqa’ who narrates about wiping over socks - he said: I heard Marra Al-Hamadani, he said: I heard Abdullah say about this verse: You will surely ascend from level to level he said: the sky. Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me: Ali bin Ghurab told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: It is the sky becoming dusty, red, and cracked. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding His statement: You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: It is the sky cracking, then turning red, then bursting. He said: Ibn Abbas said: One state after another. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah recited the letter You will surely ascend from one level to another, and he said: The sky is one state after another, and one station after another. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah You will surely ascend from one level to another, he said: It is the sky. Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Farwa, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he read it in the accusative case and said: It is the sky. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: It is the sky changing color after color. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as La tarkaban with a ta’ and with a damma on the ba’, as a way of addressing all people, that they will ride through difficult situations one situation after another. Some of them mentioned that he read it with a ya’ and with a damma on the ba’, as a way of reporting from all people, that they will do that. The most correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read with the ta’ and with the ba’ open, because the interpretation of all the people of interpretation has been reported in this way, even though there are understandable aspects to the other readings. If the correct reading in this regard is what we have mentioned, then the correct interpretation is the saying of those who said: You will surely ride, O Muhammad, from one state to another, and from one matter to another of hardships. And what is meant, even though the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is all people, that they will encounter hardships and terrors of the Day of Resurrection in various states. We said: What we meant by that is what we mentioned, that the speech before his saying You will surely ascend level upon level was addressed to everyone, and likewise after it, so it was more likely that it was similar to what came before and after it. His saying: Level upon layer is from the Arab saying: So-and-so fell into the daughters of a layer meaning he fell into a difficult matter.
84:20: And His statement: So why do they not believe? God Almighty says: So why do these polytheists not believe in the Oneness of God, nor acknowledge the resurrection after death, when their Lord has sworn to them that they will ride one level after another, despite what they have witnessed of His proofs of the truth of His Oneness. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So why do they not believe? He said: With this hadith, and with this matter.
84:21: And His statement: And when the Qur’an is recited to them, they do not prostrate themselves. God Almighty says: And when the Book of their Lord is recited to them, they do not submit or humble themselves. We have already explained the meaning of prostration before with its evidence, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.
84:22: His statement: Rather, those who disbelieve deny the signs of God and His revelation. God Almighty says: Rather, those who disbelieve deny the signs of God and His revelation.
84:23: And His statement: And God knows best what they conceal. God Almighty says: And God knows best what these polytheists conceal in their hearts of denial of the Book of God and His Messenger. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, they conceal, he said: they conceal. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And God knows best what they conceal, he said: A person conceals his goods and his wealth, this one in this, and this one in that, so God knows what they conceal of deeds, and the bad deeds are what their hearts conceal, and in them come together of these deeds good and evil, so the hearts are the receptacle of all of these deeds, good and evil, He knows what they conceal and what they declare, and He has concealed for you that which no one knows whether it is from the Qur’an or other than that, so fear God and beware of introducing some of this evil into the noble deeds of these deeds, which spoils them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, they are aware, he said, in their chests.
84:24: And His saying: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. God Almighty says: So give tidings, O Muhammad, to these deniers of God’s signs, of a painful punishment for them from God, which will be painful.
84:25: God Almighty says: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds meaning: Except for those of them who repented and believed, and acknowledged His Oneness, and the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the resurrection after death. And do righteous deeds meaning: And fulfilled God’s obligations, and avoided doing what God forbade them to do. And His statement: For them is a reward uninterrupted. God Almighty says: For those who believe and do righteous deeds, there is a reward that is not calculated or diminished. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, For them is a reward uninterrupted, meaning: undiminished. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, an unaccounted reward means: not calculated.
